authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: The company closed its acquisition of a 60% equity interest in Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center business, after the fiscal year-end. Brightray became a consolidated subsidiary and is not in the FY2026 statements.
The company completed a first closing of its private placement, selling 1,000,000 Purchaser Units for gross proceeds of US$10,000,000.
A 10-for-1 forward share subdivision took effect, and Class A shares began trading on a split-adjusted basis.

business_model.basis: Stated in Items 4 and 5 of the 20-F.
business_model.claim: The company sells meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions (MICE) services in Hong Kong. The services fall into two areas: event management (design, planning, project management, on-site supervision) and stage production.
quotes: our service portfolio comprised two core areas: (i) event management and (ii) stage production

business_model.basis: Stated in the revenue breakdown table (US$) and in Item 4.
business_model.claim: Event management is the larger revenue line. In the year ended June 30, 2026 it was 5,567,719 (US$) of total revenue of 6,651,132, about 83.7%. Stage production made up the rest.
quotes: Our revenue derived from event management services represents approximately 83.7%, 83.4% and 80.5% of our total revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: Customers are third parties in Hong Kong, and all revenue in the periods presented came from Hong Kong. Customer concentration is high: the largest customer was about 50.7% of FY2026 revenue, against 27.9% and 29.1% in the two prior years.
quotes: We generated all of our revenue during the fiscal years presented in Hong Kong, from third parties, through the provision of event management and stage production services.
Our largest customer accounted for approximately 50.7%, 27.9% and 29.1% of our revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: Revenue is project-based, not recurring. Clients engage the company per project with no long-term contracts, and quotes are set on a cost-plus margin basis. Customers are granted credit terms of 60 to 90 days.
quotes: We offer our MICE services to clients on an individual project basis and typically do not enter into long-term contracts with them.
we generally derive our revenue from service contracts, with each contract sum being determined with reference to quotations that are formulated on a cost-plus margin basis
For our MICE services, we typically grant our customers a credit period ranging from 60 to 90 days from the invoice date.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Item 5 discussion and the income statement.
business_model.claim: Revenue rose 5.1% in FY2026, to 6,651,132 from 6,328,425. Management attributes the rise mainly to event management, through more and larger projects.
quotes: The growth was mainly attributable to an increase in the number of event management projects and the larger scale of those projects.

business_model.claim: Cost of revenue has three components: purchase costs (furniture, equipment, supplies, transportation), labor costs and subcontracting costs. Purchase costs were 2,647,597 in FY2026, or 48.0% of cost of revenue, and rose about 62.3% as inflation and larger stage-equipment needs hit. Gross margin fell from about 31.0% to about 17.0%.
quotes: The decrease in our gross profit margin was mainly due to the increase in cost of revenue being proportionately larger than the increase in revenue

business_model.claim: Fees are largely fixed once a contract is signed, so the company bears cost overruns. This makes cost management central to project profitability.
quotes: our service fee will be fixed once the contract has been signed and any additional costs incurred during the service period would be borne by us

business_model.basis: Stated in the income statement, cash flow statement and Item 5.
business_model.claim: FY2026 swung to an operating loss of (4,851,223) because general administrative expenses jumped to $5,981,844. These included share-based compensation of $3,979714 versus nil a year earlier, a non-cash item in the cash flow statement.
quotes: Share-based compensation was $3,979,714 for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to nil for the year ended June 30, 2025.

business_model.claim: Demand is seasonal. The company saw higher demand around Easter, the summer holiday and Christmas, while fixed costs such as rent and staff remain in the quieter months.
quotes: we experienced higher demands for our services during Easter, the summer holiday, and Christmas

business_model.basis: Stated in Items 4 and 5. How Brightray earns revenue is not described in the excerpts.
business_model.claim: After year-end the company acquired a 60% stake in Brightray, which provides prefabricated modular data center solutions. The deal closed on September 15, 2026. Brightray is not in the FY2026 results, so the historical figures describe only the MICE business.
quotes: Brightray’s operating results are not included in our consolidated results for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1 and P3; the positioning language is the company's self-description
competitive_position.claim: The operating business is a Hong Kong MICE provider, with event management as the larger of its two service lines at 83.7% of revenue in the latest fiscal year.
quotes: Established in 2017, we have rapidly grown into a premier MICE solutions provider based in Hong Kong.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the income statement F2; the growth reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Revenue grew modestly over three fiscal years, from 5,812,204 to 6,328,425 to 6,651,132 USD, which suggests the client franchise has held up.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 (management discussion); the pricing-power reading is inferred
competitive_position.claim: Pricing power looks weak: gross margin fell from approximately 31.0% to approximately 17.0%. Purchase costs rose 62.3% against revenue growth of 5.1%, and the company says the higher costs were not fully passed on to customers.
quotes: which were not fully passed on to customers

competitive_position.claim: Customer concentration is a named threat: the largest customer was approximately 50.7% of revenue in the latest year, up from 27.9% and 29.1% in the two prior years.
quotes: Our largest customer accounted for approximately 50.7%, 27.9% and 29.1% of our revenue for the years ended June 30, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P3 and P2 (risk factors)
competitive_position.claim: The company names a competitive market with low entry barriers and possible aggressive pricing, which threatens its gross margin.
quotes: Relatively low barriers to entry have resulted in numerous market participants competing for similar customers and projects.
The highly competitive and fragmented market for our MICE services may continue to create adverse price pressures.

competitive_position.claim: Revenue is project-based with no long-term customer contracts, so customer retention is not locked in.
quotes: We offer our MICE services to clients on an individual project basis and typically do not enter into long-term contracts with them.

competitive_position.claim: The company has no long-term supply contracts, and fees are largely fixed once a project is awarded, so supplier price increases can squeeze margin.
quotes: Our Operating Subsidiaries do not enter into long-term supply contracts with its suppliers or subcontractors

competitive_position.basis: stated in F2, F3 and P3
competitive_position.claim: The latest year swung to a loss from operations of (4,851,223) from a profit of 1,028,500. Share-based compensation of 3,979,714 was a major driver, and operating cash flow stayed slightly positive at 15,939.
quotes: Share-based compensation was $3,979,714 for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to nil for the year ended June 30, 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in F1, F3 and P3
competitive_position.claim: Financial capacity improved after the IPO: cash rose to 3,755,687 from 101,535, helped by IPO proceeds of 5,804,648. Bank borrowings of 358,021 are repayable on demand, and 1,600,000 is held as deposits for investments.
quotes: The loan agreements contain repayment-on-demand clauses, and the entire outstanding balances were classified as current liabilities.

competitive_position.claim: The company is moving beyond MICE by acquiring 60% of Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center provider. The company says this business differs significantly from its historical business, and Brightray's results are not in the reported financials.
quotes: Brightray’s business differs significantly from our historical MICE business in Hong Kong.

competitive_position.claim: The Brightray deal is paid in newly issued shares and a P-Note settled in shares, which the company says would dilute existing shareholders. The cap is 24,000,000 Class A shares (240,000,000 after the split), and the P-Note has an initial face amount of US$200,000,000.
quotes: would dilute the economic and voting interests of our existing shareholders

competitive_position.claim: Brightray's disclosed pipeline is non-binding: the Macao framework agreement for about 40MW creates no purchase or supply obligation, and the Indiana letter of intent for about 10MW is also non-binding.
quotes: The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

competitive_position.claim: Integration of Brightray is a named threat to the existing MICE business, because it will absorb management attention.
quotes: Integration will require significant management attention and resources and may divert attention from our MICE business.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet and the MD&A liquidity section.
financial_health.claim: Liquidity improved sharply over the latest fiscal year. Cash rose to $3,755,687 from $101,535, and current assets of 5,406,820 exceed current liabilities of 1,798,376 (balance-sheet figures in USD).
quotes: As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $3,755,687 and $101,535, respectively.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement.
financial_health.claim: The cash increase was funded by financing. Net cash from financing was 5,240,035, including 5,804,648 of IPO proceeds net of offering cost. Operating cash flow was only 15,939, against 336,061 in the prior year.

financial_health.basis: Inferred from the reconciliation lines in the cash flow statement and the income statement.
financial_health.claim: Cash generation is of low quality. The net loss of 4,813,197 turned into slightly positive operating cash flow only because of 3,979,714 of non-cash share-based compensation and working-capital inflows, such as a 493,332 reduction in trade receivables and a 411,414 increase in trade payables.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the income statement and the MD&A.
financial_health.claim: Operating profitability deteriorated. The loss from operations was 4,851,223 against a profit of 1,028,500 in the prior year. Gross margin fell from about 31.0% to about 17.0% on higher purchase costs, and general administrative expenses rose to 5,981,844.
quotes: Our gross profit margin decreased from approximately 31.0% for the year ended June 30, 2025 to approximately 17.0% for the year ended June 30, 2026.

financial_health.claim: Leverage is low. Total liabilities were 2,178,082 against total equity of 5,595,146. Bank borrowings were 358,021, all current, and finance lease liabilities were 49,454 current and 42,024 non-current.

financial_health.basis: Stated for the clauses and classification; the coverage by cash is inferred from the balance sheet.
financial_health.claim: All bank borrowings of 358,021 fall due on demand and are classed as current. Cash of 3,755,687 is many times that amount, so the debt can be met from cash on hand. The company repaid 86,144 of bank borrowings in the year.
quotes: The loan agreements contain repayment-on-demand clauses, and the entire outstanding balances were classified as current liabilities.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the going concern note and the MD&A.
financial_health.claim: Management states that existing cash, expected operating cash flows and available financing are adequate for at least twelve months. Its financial statements are prepared on a going concern basis.
quotes: Management believes that the Company’s existing cash resources, together with expected cash flows from operations and available financing sources, provide adequate financial resources to continue as a going concern for at least twelve months from the date these consolidated financial statements are issued.

financial_health.basis: Stated in the balance sheet and the MD&A; the link to the PINK 308 LLC memorandum of understanding is not established.
financial_health.claim: A cash commitment is pending. 1,600,000 of refundable deposits for equity investments in a private Delaware company sit in non-current assets, outside cash and working capital, and the expected closing date has been extended once.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026, we also held $1,600,000 of refundable deposits for pending equity investments in a private company incorporated in Delaware.

financial_health.claim: After year-end the company completed a first closing of a private placement with gross proceeds of US$10,000,000. The Brightray acquisition is paid in shares and a share-settled P-Note, not cash. This adds liquidity and potential dilution, not debt.
quotes: The P-Note is settled solely in Class A Ordinary Shares at the fixed issue price in annual instalments determined by reference to Brightray’s Net Profit

growth_thesis.basis: Revenue figures are stated in the income statement. The driver is stated in Item 5. The continuation condition is inferred from the project-based risk factor and the customer concentration disclosure.
growth_thesis.claim: Core MICE revenue has grown for three years, to 6,651,132 from 6,328,425 and 5,812,204, with the latest rise tied to more and larger event management projects. For this to continue, customers must keep commissioning projects.
quotes: The growth was mainly attributable to an increase in the number of event management projects and the larger scale of those projects.

growth_thesis.basis: Margin figures and the cause are stated in Item 5. The condition is inferred from that explanation.
growth_thesis.claim: The core business grew revenue but not profit. Gross profit fell to 1,130,621 from 1,963,514, and gross margin fell to 17.0% from 31.0%. For core growth to add profit, cost increases must be passed on to customers.
quotes: which were not fully passed on to customers

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the balance sheet, cash flow statement and liquidity discussion. The condition on deployment is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: The IPO raised cash that funds expansion. Cash rose to $3,755,687 from $101,535, helped by net IPO proceeds of 5,804,648. For this to support growth, the cash must be deployed productively, because operating cash flow was only 15,939.
quotes: As of June 30, 2026 and 2025, we had cash and cash equivalents of $3,755,687 and $101,535, respectively.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 4 and the risk factors. No Brightray financial figures are in the packet.
growth_thesis.claim: The main stated growth step is the acquisition of a 60% interest in Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center provider. It closed after the fiscal year end, so none of its results are in the reported figures. The benefit depends on integrating a business that differs significantly from the MICE business.
quotes: As the Acquisition was completed after June 30, 2026, the results of Brightray are not included in our consolidated financial statements for the year ended June 30, 2026 included in this annual report.

growth_thesis.claim: Brightray's value to the company depends on its Net Profit. DeedTech guarantees cumulative Net Profit of not less than US$150 million, and any shortfall reduces the consideration.
quotes: DeedTech has guaranteed that such cumulative Net Profit will be not less than US$150 million, and any shortfall reduces the consideration, including, following the final determination, through the surrender of Class A Ordinary Shares previously issued in settlement of the P-Note.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 4 and the risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: The remaining share consideration for Brightray is released only in stages, as cash is collected and after Brightray's core trade marks and intellectual property are transferred or licensed. Brightray's operating base therefore depends on that IP transfer being completed.
quotes: no Class A Ordinary Shares are issuable after the Consideration Shares until the core trade marks used in Brightray’s business have been transferred to, and licences of its other core intellectual property have been granted to, the Brightray group.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 4 and the risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: The acquisition is paid for in shares, not cash. The 60% interest is capped at 24,000,000 Class A shares, or 240,000,000 after the share subdivision. Growth through Brightray therefore comes with dilution of existing holders.
quotes: The aggregate number of Class A Ordinary Shares issuable under the Share Purchase Agreement for our 60% equity interest, inclusive of the Consideration Shares, is capped at 24,000,000 Class A Ordinary Shares (240,000,000 after giving effect to the Share Subdivision).

growth_thesis.claim: A private placement gave first-closing gross proceeds of US$10,000,000, which the company intends to use for Brightray's capacity expansion and working capital. Further closings of up to 2,000,000 units, or 20,000,000 after the split, were allowed.
quotes: We intend to use the proceeds of the Private Placement for capacity expansion and working capital requirements in connection with the expansion of the business of Brightray.

growth_thesis.claim: A Macao data center framework agreement of about 40MW of IT capacity is a possible Brightray order source. It is non-binding, and a definitive contract depends on the customer first securing a tenant.
quotes: The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 4. The condition on the purchase order is inferred from the non-binding terms.
growth_thesis.claim: An Indiana letter of intent for a prefabricated data center of about 10MW is Brightray's first U.S. project letter of intent. Its principal cooperation terms are non-binding, so growth from it depends on a purchase order actually being issued.
quotes: The principal cooperation terms of the letter of intent are non-binding and do not create any obligation to purchase, supply or pay, and the letter of intent will expire 12 months after signing unless replaced earlier by a definitive agreement.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in Item 4, Item 5 and the balance sheet. The link between the deposits and PINK 308 is not stated.
growth_thesis.claim: A possible acquisition of PINK 308 LLC, a holding company for film assets, is another growth option. It is only a non-binding memorandum of understanding, and its expected closing has been pushed back. The company holds 1,600,000 in refundable deposits for pending equity investments.
quotes: The memorandum of understanding does not constitute a definitive agreement, and the terms of any transaction, including consideration, structure and timing, remain subject to due diligence, negotiation and definitive documentation.

material_events.claim: The company closed its acquisition of a 60% equity interest in Brightray, a prefabricated modular data center business, after the fiscal year-end. Brightray became a consolidated subsidiary and is not in the FY2026 statements.
quotes: The Acquisition closed on September 15, 2026, and Brightray became our consolidated subsidiary.

material_events.claim: The company completed a first closing of its private placement, selling 1,000,000 Purchaser Units for gross proceeds of US$10,000,000.
quotes: we completed a first closing of 1,000,000 Purchaser Units (10,000,000 Purchaser Units after giving effect to the Share Subdivision) for gross proceeds of US$10,000,000

material_events.claim: A 10-for-1 forward share subdivision took effect, and Class A shares began trading on a split-adjusted basis.
quotes: The Share Subdivision became effective, and our Class A Ordinary Shares began trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market on a split-adjusted basis, at market open on October 26, 2026, under a new CUSIP number G1739L110.

material_events.claim: The company announced that it intends to relocate its corporate headquarters from Hong Kong to Singapore. The principal executive office remains in Hong Kong as of the annual report date.
quotes: On September 3, 2026, we announced that we intend to relocate our corporate headquarters from Hong Kong to Singapore.

material_events.claim: The company signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding to explore acquiring PINK 308 LLC, a film and screenplay asset holding company. The acquisition remains pending and its expected closing date was extended.
quotes: On May 4, 2026, we entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding with the owners of PINK 308 LLC to explore a potential acquisition of PINK 308 LLC, a holding company being established for a portfolio of film, in-production film and screenplay assets.

material_events.claim: A Brightray subsidiary signed a framework agreement with a customer for a planned data center project in Macao. The agreement is non-binding and creates no purchase or supply obligation.
quotes: Brightray Veridian Pte. Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary of Brightray, entered into a prefabricated module sales framework agreement with a customer
The framework agreement does not create any obligation to purchase or supply modules, and pricing under it is provisional and non-binding.

material_events.claim: A Brightray subsidiary signed a non-binding letter of intent with a U.S. partner for a planned prefabricated data center project in Indiana.
quotes: Brightray Veridian Pte. Ltd. entered into a letter of intent with a U.S.-based mission critical infrastructure partner

The principal cooperation terms of the letter of intent are non-binding and do not create any obligation to purchase, supply or pay, and the letter of intent will expire 12 months after signing unless replaced earlier by a definitive agreement.

material_events.claim: The company closed its Nasdaq initial public offering of 1,500,000 Class A shares at US$4.00 per share. A partial over-allotment exercise followed.
quotes: On August 15, 2025, the Company closed its initial public offering of 1,500,000 Class A Ordinary Shares at a public offering price of US$4.00 per share on the Nasdaq.

risks.basis: Stated in the Item 3.D risk factor; the mechanism is partly inferred from the risk text.
risks.claim: The company is moving from a Hong Kong events business into prefabricated data centers through the Brightray acquisition, and Brightray's results are not in the reported financials. Integration could fail or the business could underperform.
quotes: Brightray’s business differs significantly from our historical MICE business in Hong Kong.

risks.basis: Stated in the Item 4 and Item 3.D passages.
risks.claim: Settling the P-Note and any further acquisition consideration in new Class A shares could substantially dilute existing holders. The share issuance is capped at 24,000,000 shares (240,000,000 after the subdivision), and the uplift for late issuance sits outside the cap.
quotes: Any issuance of Class A Ordinary Shares in settlement of the P-Note, and any consideration payable in Class A Ordinary Shares for the remaining 40% interest in Brightray if we exercise our call option, would dilute the economic and voting interests of our existing shareholders.

risks.basis: Cash figures are stated in F1, F3 and P3; the liquidity-pressure inference is analyst reasoning. Management's contrary conclusion is stated in P4.
risks.claim: Operating cash flow was very small, and the year-end cash of $3,755,687 came from IPO proceeds rather than operations. The company reported a net loss, holds a refundable deposit, and has bank borrowings repayable on demand.
quotes: Management believes that the Company’s existing cash resources, together with expected cash flows from operations and available financing sources, provide adequate financial resources to continue as a going concern for at least twelve months from the date these consolidated financial statements are issued.

risks.basis: Concentration percentage stated in P3; the project-based contract nature is stated in P2.

risks.basis: Stated in the Item 5 discussion and the income statement.
